title: Outlook: folder sharing respects organisation restrictions on Default and Anonymous permissions
summary: The briefing passes: its planned behaviour and rollout facts match the roadmap, and Microsoft documents the existing controls it describes. Minor corrections should complete the Cloud Policy path, acknowledge conflicting publish-button instructions, and distinguish unpublished feature-specific licensing from Outlook's published product licensing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: For Exchange Online calendars, Default applies to authenticated organisation users without an explicit permission entry.
claims.quote: Default applies to authenticated users in the organization who don't have an explicit permission entry.

claims.claim: For Exchange Online calendars, Anonymous applies to unauthenticated callers without access through a calendar-sharing relationship.
claims.quote: Anonymous applies to callers who aren't authenticated and don't have access through a calendar-sharing relationship.

claims.claim: The calendar-permissions article gives AvailabilityOnly as Default's typical value.
claims.quote: Default applies to authenticated users in the organization who don't have an explicit permission entry. Its typical value is AvailabilityOnly.

claims.claim: The calendar-permissions article gives None as Anonymous's typical value.
claims.quote: Anonymous applies to callers who aren't authenticated and don't have access through a calendar-sharing relationship. Its typical value is None.

claims.claim: Increasing Anonymous above None can expose calendar information more broadly than intended.
claims.quote: Increasing Anonymous above None can expose calendar information more broadly than intended.

claims.claim: The existing folder-permission Cloud Policy control is reached in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center through Customization > Policy Management.
claims.quote: To view a list of policy configurations, select Customization > Policy Management.
claims.fix: Complete controls[0].ui.path as 'Customization > Policy Management > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings'. Retain the note naming the three settings to enable. The remaining route is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy, which is already cited.

claims.claim: The documented Cloud Policy route restricts folder-permission changes in classic Outlook, new Outlook and Outlook on the web.
claims.quote: Restrict users from changing folder permissions in classic Outlook, new Outlook, and Outlook on the Web

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A Cloud Policy configuration is scoped to users and can target specific groups.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.claim: The documented existing Cloud Policy procedure enables Turn off sharing recommendation.
claims.quote: Enable each of the following policies: Turn off sharing recommendation

claims.claim: The documented existing Cloud Policy procedure enables Do not allow users to change permissions on folders.
claims.quote: Do not allow users to change permissions on folders

claims.claim: The documented existing Cloud Policy procedure enables Control Calendar Sharing.
claims.quote: Control Calendar Sharing

claims.claim: The existing folder-permission procedure creates a policy configuration and selects its applicable scope before enabling the settings.
claims.quote: Create a new policy configuration, and select the applicable scope.

claims.claim: After creating the folder-permission policy configuration, the procedure says to select Update.
claims.quote: To apply the policy configuration, select Update.
claims.fix: Replace the note's final 'select Update' with 'The folder-permission article says to select Update; the Cloud Policy overview says Create for a new configuration and Review and publish > Update for changes to an existing configuration.' The differing instructions are at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy.

claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 API PowerShell create update policy configuration folder permissions. Read Cloud Policy overview and restricting-folder-permissions article; no operation configuring these Cloud policies found.

claims.claim: Set DisableEditPermissions and DisableEditDefaultUserPermissions to 1 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Options\Folders.
claims.quote: set the value of the following registry entries to 1: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Options\Folders\DisableEditPermissions; HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Office\16.0\Outlook\Options\Folders\DisableEditDefaultUserPermissions

claims.claim: The two registry values have DWORD (32-bit) type.
claims.quote: When you create the DisableEditPermissions and DisableEditDefaultUserPermissions values, set their type to DWORD (32-bit).

claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing is not yet published, represented by the licensing model unknown.
claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace licensing.notes with 'Outlook for Windows with a Microsoft 365 organisational email address requires a plan that includes desktop Microsoft 365 apps, such as Microsoft 365 Business Standard or Microsoft 365 Business Premium. Once an account with a qualifying licence is added, secondary accounts need not include desktop apps. Feature-specific licensing and a meter for this item are not yet published (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/get-started/licensing-options and use the same product-level qualification in Cost and licensing; retain the low cost rating.
